steps.action:
The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering, in which sunlight interacts with gas molecules in Earth's atmosphere and scatters in all directions. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than other colors in the visible spectrum, causing it to scatter far more efficiently than longer-wavelength colors like red or yellow. When you look at any part of the sky away from the sun, this scattered blue light is what predominantly reaches your eyes, making the sky appear blue.
